questions.question: A concave mirror is made from a section of the surface of a sphere of radius 18.0 cm. According to New Cartesian Sign Convention, its principal focus is located at x = _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **-9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **New Cartesian Sign Convention**

 
 
• Because the** object **is always in front of the mirror, its distance is counted as **negative.**
 
• Since the concave mirror's **center of curvature and focus** are in front of it, the concave mirror's focal length and radius of curvature are considered **negative.**
 
• When an** image** is formed** in front of the mirror**, the **distance **between the two is taken as **–**, which indicates a **negative image**, while the **distance** between the two is taken as **+**, which indicates a **positive image.**
 
• In the case of an upright image, the** height of the image** is taken as** positive**, whereas in an **inverted image**, it is taken as **negative.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calculation**

 
 
• **Concave mirror,**

 Radius of curvature= 18 cm

 We know, Principal Focus is half of radius of curvature. 

 So, f= 18/2= 9cm

 Now, According to** New Cartesian Sign Convention**

 The concave mirror's focal length is considered negative.

 **So, the principal focus will be -9cm.**

__
 
• **Food Chain**

 
 
• The sequence of events in an** ecosystem** is known as a food chain. In a food chain, one living organism eats another living organism, which is then eaten by another larger living organism.
 
• A food chain is the **movement of energy and nutrients** from one organism to another at various trophic levels.
 
• The feeding pattern or relationship between living things is also explained by the food chain.
 
• **Trophic level** describes the order in which producers at the bottom of a food chain are followed by **primary, secondary, and tertiary consumers.**
 
• A trophic level is the name given to each level in a food chain.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major parts of food chain**

 
 
• **The Sun**:

 
 
• The sun is the first place that **energy comes from**, and it powers everything on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Producers**:
 
 
• All autotrophs, including **phytoplankton, cyanobacteria, algae, and green plants**, are producers in a food chain.
 
• A food chain begins at this point. The first level of a food chain is made up of producers. Food is produced by producers using the sun's energy.
 
• Because producers produce their own food, they are also known as **autotrophs**. Any plant or other organism that uses photosynthesis to make its own nutrients are producers.
 
 
 
• **Consumers**:
 
 
• All organisms that rely on plants or other organisms for food are consumers. Due to the presence of nearly every living thing, this is the largest component of a** food web**.
 
• It includes **herbivores**, which eat plants, carnivores, which eat other animals, parasites, which live on other organisms by harming them, and **scavengers**, which eat the carcasses of dead animals.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers**:
 
 
• Organisms known as decomposers extract energy from **decaying or waste organic material**. A food chain ends at this point.
 
• Decomposers are an essential component of a food chain because they** transform organic waste into inorganic materials**, adding nutrients to the soil or land.

questions.question: Which element is neither metal nor non-metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Ge.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Germanium (Ge)**

 
 
• The chemical element germanium has the** atomic number 32 **and the symbol Ge. It has a **grayish-white lustre**, is **hard and brittle**, and looks like silicon.
 
• It is a **metalloid** in the carbon group with chemical similarities to silicon and tin, its group neighbors. In nature, germanium, like silicon, naturally reacts with oxygen to form complexes.
 
• Since germanium rarely occurs in large quantities, it was discovered relatively late in the discovery of the elements.
 
• In terms of the relative abundance of the elements in the Earth's crust, germanium ranks near the** top fifty.**
 
• From its position on his periodic table, **Dmitri Mendeleev** predicted its existence and some of its properties in **1869**, and he named the element **eka silicon.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum (Al)**

 
 
• The chemical element aluminum, or aluminum in North American English, has the **atomic number 13** and the symbol Al.
 
• The density of aluminum is approximately one third that of steel, making it **less dense** than other common metals.
 
• When **exposed to air**, it forms a protective oxide layer on the surface and has a **strong affinity for oxygen.**
 
• Both in terms of its color and its remarkable ability to reflect light, aluminum has a visual resemblance to silver. It is **flexible, non-magnetic, and soft. **
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus (P)**
 
 
• The chemical element phosphorus has the **atomic number 15**, and the symbol P. **White phosphorus and red phosphorus** are the two main forms of elemental phosphorus.
 
• However, due to its** high reactivity**, phosphorus is never found as a free element on Earth.
 
• It has a concentration of about one gram per kilogram in the Earth's crust, compared to that of **copper**, which is about 0.06 grams. Phosphorus is typically found in minerals as phosphate.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)**
 
 
• The chemical element magnesium has the **atomic number 12 **and the symbol Mg. It is a **shiny gray metal with a low density**, a high chemical reactivity, and a low melting point.
 
• It almost always has an **oxidation state of +2**, like the other alkaline earth metals in group 2 of the periodic table, which only occur naturally when combined with other elements.
 
• It readily reacts with air to form a **magnesium oxide** passivation coating that prevents the metal from corroding further.

__
 
• **Magnetic field lines**

 
 
• **​**The **magnet or moving electric charges** create a field known as the magnetic field. The region within which the force of magnetism operates around a magnetic substance or **moving electric charge** is known as the magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/175de06bdbbf9738b8d7f0ca3ec60fb626e04dc1856f10ee60f1f51e2c9953fe.png]

• Mark the direction that the compass needle is pointing in after you have checked it.
 
• Mark the directions by moving the compass needle to **various positions.** The lines of the magnetic field can be seen by joining the points.

__
 
• **Joule’s Law of Heating**

 
 
• **​**The factors that determine how much heat is produced in a conductor when an **electric current** flows through it are described by Joule's law of heating. Let's say that for a given **time (t)**, a resistor with a **resistance of R** experiences **current (I).**
 
• The resistor's heat energy dissipation capacity will be determined by **H= I²Rt**
 
• The heat produced or dissipated in a resistor is
 
 
• (i) directly proportional to the **square of the current flowing** through the resistor,
 
• (ii) directly proportional to the **resistance** for a given current, and
 
• (iii) directly proportional to the **time **the current flows through the resistance. This is referred to as Joules' law of heating.
 
 
 
• The following statements can be drawn from Joule's law of heating:
 
 
• The amount of **heat** produced will **quadruple** if the current flowing through a **resistor is doubled.**
 
• The amount of **heat** produced will also **double** if the conductor's **resistance is doubled**. Similarly, when the conductor's resistance is reduced to half, the amount of heat it produces is reduced to half.
 
• The amount of **heat** produced **doubles** if the amount of** time t**he current travel through the conductor is **doubled**.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Electric Bulb**:

 
 
• The filament of an electric bulb is made of **tungsten**. Because the **melting point of tungsten is 3380°C**, tungsten wire has a high resistance and can withstand a lot of heat.
 
• When electricity is passed through the bulb's filament, it gets **very hot and glows** because its temperature rises to **2500°C**.
 
• If we place our hand below the bulb, we can easily feel the **heat** that is produced by its filament without actually touching it.
 
• An electric bulb is filled with a mixture of **argon and nitrogen** to prolong the life of the tungsten filament and prevent its corrosion.
 
 
 
• **Electric Fuse**:
 
 
• A safety device, an electric fuse, is **effective**. It **prevents damage** to the household appliances connected to the **circuit from overloading or short-circuiting**.
 
• It operates on the electric current's heating effect. It usually consists of a** thin wire made of a lead-tin alloy**.
 
• It resists very little. It is connected to the circuit in series. A fuse wire melts when exposed to an excessive amount of current.
 
• This interrupts the circuit and prevents damage to the** appliances that are connected to it.**

questions.question: Four bells ring at intervals of 4 minutes, 8 minutes, 12 minutes and 24 minutes respectively. All the four bells rang together at 12 noon. How many times after 12 noon will all the four bells ring together in the next four hours, with the ringing at 4 p.m. being included?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Common interval = LCM(4, 8, 12, 24) = 24 minutes.

Total time duration = 4 p.m. − 12 noon = 4 hours.

Total minutes = 4 × 60 = 240 minutes.

Number of times after 12 noon = 240 ÷ 24 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 times.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Bells ringing intervals = 4 min, 8 min, 12 min, 24 min.

Initial time = 12 noon.

End time = 4 p.m.

**Formula Used:**

Next occurrence = Start time + LCM of intervals.

Number of occurrences = Total duration ÷ LCM.

 
• 
 
 12:00 (Start)

 Interval = 24 mins (LCM)
 Total 10 rings after start

 ...

⇒ LCM of 4, 8, 12, 24:

⇒ 4 = 2²

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3 = 24 minutes.

⇒ Total duration = 4 hours = 4 × 60 = 240 minutes.

⇒ Number of times ringing together after 12 noon = 240 ÷ 24 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 times.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM for Periodic Events

For objects moving or ringing at different intervals, the first time they meet/ring together again is the LCM of their individual time periods.

Including vs. Excluding Start Point

If the question asks for total times including the first ringing, use (Total Time ÷ LCM) + 1. If it asks for times "after" the start, use (Total Time ÷ LCM).

Always ensure all time units (minutes, hours, seconds) are converted to a single common unit before performing LCM or division.</p

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India says that 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 21.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• Article21__

 __
 
• No one "shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty unless in accordance with a procedure established by law," according to Article 21. As a result, article 21 protects two rights: 1. The right to life, 2. The right to individual freedom.
 
• The Indian Constitution's Article 21 was established by the Government of India Act, 1935. It states that no one may be robbed of their life or personal freedom until doing so in accordance with the legal process. One of the essential freedoms that all Indian citizens are entitled to is Article 21, which is found in Part III of the Indian Constitution. Several rights and liberties that are a part of Article 21 will be covered in this article.
 
• Article 21A declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years. It is added by the 86th Constitution Amendment Act, 2002. 
 
• The right to life in Article 21 of Indian constitution does not mean animal existence or the mere act of breathing. It guarantees the right to a dignified life.
 
 
 
• History Judgements-
 
 
• Kharak Singh vs. the State of UP and Others: Right to privacy was included in Article 21 by this case.
 
• Sunil Batra vs. Delhi Administration: In this case, Supreme Court deemed the fatal handcuffs for the convicted persons as unconstitutional as it suggests inhuman behavior towards the prisoner. The court reiterated the clause “protection to the convicted and accused person” under Article 21.
 
• Mohini Jain vs. the State of Karnataka, 1992 SC: The SC held that the Right to life also includes the Right to education. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution: Important Cases

 
 
• 1951's A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras In this case, the Supreme Court has applied a strict reading of Article 21. It was decided that only arbitrary executive activity is covered by Article 21's protection, not arbitrary legislative action. This indicates that a legislation may be used by the state to deny a person the rights guaranteed by Article 21.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of 'fiat' money in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Rs. 1000 cheque.__

__
 
• Fiat money __

 __
 
• Government-issued currency known as "fiat money" is not backed by a physical good like gold. Because they can manage the amount of money printed, central banks using fiat money have more power over the economy. The majority of contemporary paper currencies, including the dollar, are fiat currencies.
 
• Fiat money, which was introduced as a replacement for representational money and commodity money, has a value based on supply and demand.
 
• Commodity money is created from precious metals such as gold and silver, while representative money represents a claim on a commodity that can be redeemed.
 
• Around the year 1000 AD, China became the first nation to employ fiat money, after which other nations began to use it as well. As a result of President Richard Nixon's law repealing the direct convertibility of the US dollar into gold, it gained popularity in the 20th century. The majority of countries currently employ paper-based fiat currencies that only serve as a mode of payment. 
 
 
 
• History of Fiat Money__
 __
 
• In the 10th century, mostly under the Yuan, Tang, Song, and Ming dynasties, China is where fiat money first appeared. Metal money was in great demand during the Tang Dynasty (618–907) and was harder to come by than precious metals. The populace was accustomed to using credit notes, and paper or paper draughts were commonly accepted.
 
• People were obliged to switch from coins to notes due to a coin shortage. The Sichuan province experienced a boom in trade during the Song Dynasty (960–1276), which resulted in a dearth of copper coins. Private notes backed by a monetary reserve were originally recognised as legal money when traders began issuing them. The only legal tender in the became paper money Yuan Dynasty (1276-1367), and issuing of notes was conferred to the Ministry of Finance during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644).
 
• According to the Bretton Woods Agreement, a troy ounce of gold is worth 35 US dollars. However, due to diminishing gold reserves, US President Richard Nixon implemented a number of economic measures in 1971, including ending the direct conversion of US dollars into gold. Since then, the majority of nations have adopted fiat currencies that can be exchanged for other significant currencies.

• Advantages and disadvantages of Fiat Money-
 
 
• 
 
In the 20th century, governments and banks intervened to shield their economies from the recurrent business cycle busts, which led to the widespread usage of fiat money.

 
Disadvantage- Currency based on commodities was unstable because of the regular business cycle and cyclical recessions. The central banks have more control over the money supply, interest rates, and liquidity since they can produce or hold paper money as needed. For instance, the Federal Reserve was able to handle the World Banking Crisis of 2008 to prevent more damage to the U.S. financial system and the global economy because to its control over the money supply and demand.

 
Advantage- The global financial crisis disproved the notion that fiat money is a more stable currency that can protect against recessions. options.text: Decreases the effect of climate change
Increases air pollution even upon judicious usage
No acidification of oceans death of aquatic animals

The correct answer is **__Increases air pollution even upon judicious usage.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Energy sources that are **not renewable are fossil fuels (which are present in a limited quantity)**.
 
• If they are not used wisely, they are exhaustible and won't last for very long.
 
• Fossil fuels are continually** created by natural processes**, but because they take millions of years to generate, they are regarded** as non-renewable resources.**
 
• Fossil fuels were created from the** rotting remains of terrestrial and marine flora and fauna** that were buried in strata under extreme pressure and heat millions of years ago. These sources are to blame for environmental contamination because carbon is the primary component of fossil fuels like **coal and petroleum.**
 
• **Coal__**
 __
 
• **​__**Coal is a fuel that resembles a black rock and contains between **70 and 90 percent carbon**.
 
• It is created when **plant deteriorates under intense heat and pressure.** The period of time when this process occurs is known as the** carboniferous age, **and the process of coal creation is known as carbonisation. One of the most significant fossil fuels utilised to produce power is coal. Mining techniques such as surface mining or **underground mining are used to remove coal from the earth. **
 
• To obtain energy, we burn coal. In rural areas, coal is mostly utilised as a home fuel to prepare meals. When coal is burned, toxic smoke is released. When subterranean plants is exposed to extremes of heat and pressure, coal is created.
 
• The formation of coal takes place in four stages which are** peat, lignite, bituminous, and anthracite.** **Coal mainly contains carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.**
 
 
 
• **__Types of coal__**
 __
 
• **Lignite**- In terms of carbon concentration, lignite is the lowest rank of coal (60–70% carbon). The youngest kind of coal deposit is this one. It is silky and comes in a variety of colours, **from black to brown**. As a result, brown coal is another name for lignite coal. Due to the higher handling and storage stability of other forms of coal, lignite is not widely used. Synthetic natural gas, power, and fertiliser products like anhydrous ammonia and ammonium sulphate are all produced using lignite.
 
• **Sub-bituminous-** When lignite is exposed to high temperatures and pressure for millions of years, the amount of oxygen and hydrogen decreases while the amount of carbon rises to 75%. Burning coal of this kind cleaner than the lignite variety, **producing less greenhouse gas emissions. Sub-bituminous coal is also used in electricity generation and in industrial processes.**
 
• 
 
**Bituminous**-Sub-bituminous coal is less dense and less black than bituminous coal. It contains bitumen, a material like tar. Its name is bituminous as a result. It can contain up to 85% carbon. The majority of the coal industry is made up of it. In addition to being used to generate energy, bituminous coal is also utilised to heat homes. In addition, it is employed in the production of cement and other industrial processes.

 
 
• 
 
**Anthracite** -Anthracite has the highest carbon content (more than 85%), making it the best type of coal or most mature coal resource. Greater difficulty than bitumen. It serves as a source of energy.** It burns in furnaces as a smokeless fuel.**

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Petroleum **__

 __
 
• 
 
**​**__Petroleum is a liquid fossil fuel with **a dark colou**r that is made up of different types of hydrocarbons. It has a high viscosity. It is a very practical form of energy. However, the petroleum recovered from oil wells is not in a form that can be used immediately**. Because it is impure, it is referred to as crude oil.**

 
 
• This crude oil is refined via a procedure called** fractional distillation**, in which different hydrocarbons separate to form different fractions. Some of its fractions include diesel, gasoline, kerosene, and paraffin. Vehicles run on gasoline as fuel. **The fractions produced by refining crude oil are used to make a number of goods, including plastics, tyres, and synthetic materials like polyester, **in addition to being utilised for transportation. It provides consistent and portable energy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information __ **

__
 
• **Conservation of petroleum and coal- __**Coal and petroleum are finite energy sources, as we all know. They won't last for more than a few decades if they aren't utilised carefully. It is vital to consider their conservation because they are employed as major energy sources all over the world. The process of conserving a resource entails utilising it more sparingly in order to extend its useful life. By using alternative or renewable energy sources, such as hydropower, wind power, geothermal power, tidal power, etc., we may save coal and petroleum. **The replacements for fossil fuels like coal and petroleum will provide us more in the future.**

alpha and beta are two roots of the equation

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ____**Section 29A**__- Registration of organisations and groups as political parties with the Election Commission (29A).

 __
 
• 
 
(1) To take advantage of the provisions of this Part, any association or group of Indian nationals identifying themselves as** political parties must apply to the Election Commission for registration as such for the purposes of this Act.**

 
 
• 
 
(2) Each such application must be submitted,—(a) if the association or body was already in existence at the time the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1988 (1 of 1989) went into effect, within sixty days after that date; (b) if the association or body was created after that date, within thirty days after that date.

 
 
• 
 
(3) The top executive officer of the association or body, whether referred to as the** Secretary or by any other title, must sign each application made pursuant to subsection (1) and present it in person or send it by registered mail to the Secretary of the Commission.**

 
 
• 
 
(4) Each of these applications must include the information listed below: (a) the name of the organisation or body; the name of its president, secretary, treasurer, and other office-holders; (b) the State in which its head office is located; (c) the address to which letters and other communications meant for it should be sent; (d) the number of its members, and if there are categories of its members, the number of members in each category; (f) whether it has any local units; if so, at what levels;

 (g) whether it is represented by any member or members in either House of Parliament or of any State Legislature; if so, the number of such member or members.

 
 
• 
 
(5) The application under subsection (1) shall be accompanied by a copy of the memorandum or rules and regulations of the association or body, by whatever name called, and such memorandum or rules and regulations shall specifically state that the association or body shall bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as established by law, to the principles of socialism, secularism, and democracy, and would uphold the sovereignty, unity, and inviolability of the country.

 
 
• 
 
(6) The Commission may request from the **association or entity any additional information it deems appropriate. **

 
 
• 
 
(7) The Commission shall decide whether to register the association or body as a political party for the purposes of this Part after taking into account all the aforementioned details in its possession and any other necessary and relevant factors, and after affording the representatives of the association or body a reasonable opportunity to be heard. The Commission shall communicate its decision to the association or body (5).

 
 
• 
 
(8) **The Commission's judgement is conclusive.**

 
 
• 
 
(9) Following the registration of an organisation or body as a political party as aforesaid, any change in its name, head office, office-bearers, address or in any other material matters shall be communicated to the Commission without delay.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Can the Election Commission deregister political parties?**

 
The Constitution or the undertaking made to it at the time of registration** cannot be used as grounds for the ECI to deregister parties. **A party may only be declared unlawful by the Central Government, if its registration was gained fraudulently, if it alters its internal constitution and notifies the** ECI that it can no longer adhere to the Indian Constitution, or if it was fraudulently registered.**
